question: Has the engine-cooling fault on Ocean Star happened before on this vessel or on others of the same class or technical manager?

input.query: MATCH (i:Incident)-[:ON_VOYAGE]->(v:Voyage)-[:OPERATED_BY]->(w:Vessel) WHERE toLower(i.type) CONTAINS 'cooling' RETURN i.evidence_id AS evidence_id, i.source_ref AS source_ref, i.type AS type, i.status AS status, i.reported_utc AS reported_utc, i.attributed_delay_hours AS hours, v.evidence_id AS voyage, w.name AS vessel, w.vessel_class AS class, w.technical_manager AS tm, w.evidence_id AS vessel_evidence
input.reason: Search cooling incidents across all vessels, by class/manager; no typed tool searches fleet-wide.

headline.text: Yes. Ocean Star had an earlier confirmed engine cooling fault on 2 Aug 2026 (INC-118, 9 h). The latest one is INC-201 on 6 Oct 2026. Ocean Pearl, a sister ship in the same class and with the same manager, had one on 9 May 2026. Silver Tern, which has the same manager but a different class, had one on 3 Jun 2026.

interpretation.text: I took the "current" fault to be INC-201 on VG-1042, reported 2026-10-06. "Same class" means Meridian 8500. "Same manager" means Harbourline Ship Management. I searched all incidents whose type contains 'cooling'.

confirmed_facts.text: Ocean Star: INC-118, an engine cooling fault on VG-0981, is Confirmed. It cost 9 h. A confirmed agent message ties it to a seawater cooling pump failure on 2 Aug.

cited_values.value: 9 h lost to a seawater cooling pump failure on 2 Aug

confirmed_facts.text: Ocean Star: INC-201, an engine cooling fault on VG-1042, is Confirmed. It cost 12 h.
Ocean Pearl (V004) has the same class and the same manager. INC-077 on VG-0866 is Confirmed. It cost 10 h.
Silver Tern (V006) is a Kestrel 4000 with the same manager, Harbourline. INC-094 on VG-0844 is Confirmed. It cost 7 h.
Ocean Starlight (V003) is an Atlas 6000 managed by Nordwave. INC-160 is Confirmed. It cost 14 h. It is a different class and a different manager, so it is not a match for this question.

unverified_reports.text: The master's noon report of 6 Oct says the main engine stopped for a seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failure. The message is unverified because it shares its origin with INC-201.

cited_values.value: Main engine stopped 0130-1330 LT due to seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failure.

unverified_reports.text: Harbourline's technical manager bulletin of 9 Oct is unverified. It says seals have failed repeatedly on Meridian 8500 vessels this year, including Ocean Star and Ocean Pearl.

cited_values.value: Following repeated seawater cooling pump mechanical seal failures on Meridian 8500 vessels this year (Ocean Star, Ocean Pearl),

inferences.text: This looks like a recurring pattern in the Meridian 8500 class, and Harbourline's fleet is also affected. Ocean Star has had two confirmed faults about two months apart, and a third Meridian 8500 incident is also confirmed. The pump-seal cause is only confirmed for the 2 Aug event.
inferences.based_on: The count of confirmed incidents of this type by vessel, class and manager. The root cause for INC-077 and INC-201 is not confirmed.

exclusions.text: Coral Crest (V005, Meridian 8500, Eastpoint) INC-041 was Dismissed, so it did not happen and I did not count it.

data_gaps.text: The messages/extra folder (45 files) was not loaded, so there may be more reports about these faults.

recommended_checks.text: Ask Harbourline whether the Ocean Pearl INC-077 and Ocean Star INC-201 faults were the same seal-failure cause. Also ask whether the 9 Oct bulletin sets out any corrective action for the class.
Find an independent confirmation of the 6 Oct stoppage, such as the engine log or the port agent. Its time zone is unknown ("LT" with no zone given).
